instructions: Answer all questions. For fill‑in‑the‑blank and short‑answer, use one word, letter, or number only.
title: Inventory Methods (Specific ID, Weighted Average, FIFO, LIFO)

questions.prompt: Which inventory system updates inventory records after every sale and purchase?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The perpetual system updates inventory continuously.

questions.prompt: Cost of goods sold = Goods available for sale – ___.
Goods available $20,000, ending inventory $6,500. Find cost of goods sold. (number only, no $)

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Specific identification traces actual cost to each item.
hints: The flow of costs exactly matches the flow of goods.
questions.prompt: Which inventory method traces the actual cost to each specific item sold?
Under the weighted‑average method, cost per unit = Total cost ÷ Total ___.

hints: Average cost = Total cost ÷ Total units.
questions.prompt: Total cost of goods available $4,500, total units 300. Find the weighted‑average cost per unit. (number only, no $)

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Under FIFO, the most recent costs stay in ending inventory.
hints: So the ones left are the newest.
questions.prompt: Under FIFO, which costs are included in ending inventory?

hints: This method uses oldest costs for ending inventory.
questions.prompt: In a period of rising prices, which method produces the lowest ending inventory value? (acronym: FIFO, LIFO, or WA)

questions.feedbackIfWrong: LIFO is not allowed under IFRS.
hints: It's allowed in the U.S. but not globally.
It assigns newest costs to COGS.
questions.prompt: Which inventory costing method is NOT allowed under international accounting standards (IFRS)?
Under LIFO, the ___ costs are assigned to cost of goods sold.
Goods available $9,000, LIFO ending inventory $3,200. Find COGS. (number only, no $)

hints: All units are valued at the same cost.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Weighted‑average uses a single average cost per unit.
questions.prompt: Which method smooths out price changes by using a single average cost?
